FRASER 2.0 (Scheller et al. 2023, AJHG) comparison with FRASER, LeafCutterMD and SPOT on patient cohorts was not retrievable as XML (publisher restriction) and is figure-based; not extracted.
No independent table compares MMSplice, CADD-Splice or AbSplice against RNA-validated variants; Drost et al. cover SpliceAI, Pangolin, SPiP and SQUIRLS only.
Drost et al. variant-type strata (Data S1 Tables S5 and S6) are not extracted.
No RNA-seq caller comparison reports false positives per sample in a table; outlier workload is figure-only in Segarra-Casas et al.
Minigene or MFASS-style proxies beyond the existing MFASS mapping were not added in this pass.

summary_proposal: Three published comparisons were added. Drost et al. (2025) scored 243 clinically ascertained variants, each tested for a splicing effect in patient RNA or by exon trapping, with four DNA-based predictors; the authors are a diagnostic laboratory, not the tool developers. On all 243 variants AUROC was 0.895 for SpliceAI, 0.885 for Pangolin, 0.830 for SPiP and 0.806 for SQUIRLS (Data S1 Table S3, rounded to three decimals). At literature thresholds sensitivity was 0.871, 0.858, 0.832 and 0.800 and specificity 0.750, 0.773, 0.761 and 0.591 (Table S4); requiring at least two of the four tools gave sensitivity 0.916 and specificity 0.727. Most in-house variants were sent for testing because another predictor (Alamut) flagged them, so negatives are mostly predicted-but-unconfirmed variants, and the article prose and Table S3 disagree on one AUPRC value. Segarra-Casas et al. (2025), independent of the tool developers, recorded which callers reported 16 known pathogenic splicing events in clinical muscle RNA-seq: FRASER with |dPSI| > 0.1 reported 13, FRASER with |dPSI| > 0.3 reported 9, FRASER2 10 (and one more only with the full cohort), rMATS-turbo 7 and LeafCutterMD 4 (Table 2). The events were established partly with these callers. Segers et al. (2026), the saseR developers, ranked 12 reported disease genes in the 119-sample Kremer fibroblast cohort: the gene ranked within the top 10 in 9 of 12 samples for saseR-junctions, in 6 of 12 for FRASER 2.0 with the autoencoder and in 7 of 12 for FRASER 2.0 with PCA (Table 2). This is the same cohort as the existing FRASER known-event recovery judgement, and several of the 12 genes are expression rather than splicing defects. All values are transcribed from the publications, not reproduced; none is a diagnostic-yield estimate, and results from different sources measure different endpoints and must not be pooled. This summary describes evidence and does not recommend a clinical workflow.
